result.text: The paper addresses whether minimizing Bellman error is a reliable surrogate for learning accurate value functions in reinforcement learning, particularly when using finite data or function approximation. The key insight is that Bellman error can misleadingly vanish or be small while the learned value remains far from the true value because cancellations between the two sides of the Bellman equation hide large errors and, with limited samples, many spurious solutions can exactly satisfy the Bellman equation. We propose CertiSelect-Unlearn: deletion-stable hyperparameter selection for machine unlearning that combines streaming IJ/approximate unlearning with bagged/hash-bagged ensembles and DP/RDP-accounted validation so that deletions up to a certified budget neither force re-tuning nor invalidate guarantees. args.text: We propose Roaming Task Routing for Diffusion (RTR-Diff), which replaces fixed sliding-window channel gating with regulated, randomized reassignment of gated channels or expert blocks across contiguous timestep windows during training. By enforcing a controlled roaming schedule that maximizes cross-window exposure while keeping most assignments local, RTR-Diff preserves high-affinity sharing among neighboring denoising tasks while regularizing against brittle, over-specialized allocations. Concretely, we initialize routing with interval clusters learned from timestep affinity and periodically resample masks under coverage and roaming-frequency constraints, optionally biasing harder (low-noise) steps to receive more capacity. This dynamic routing reduces negative transfer across disparate timesteps, speeds convergence, and enables smaller UNets to match larger baselines without adding parameters.

result.text: The paper tackles the practical challenges of applying reinforcement learning to large-scale recommender systems—specifically massive state/action spaces, high-variance stochastic environments, and sparse or unspecific reward signals—by proposing a model-based framework called GoalRec. The key insight is to disentangle environmental dynamics from reward estimation via a novel goal-conditioned universal value function that generalizes across different recommendation goals and ties value to predicted user trajectories rather than a single state-reward pair. Methodologically, GoalRec learns a high-capacity, reward-independent world model to simulate user dynamics under given goals and uses those predictions to train the disentangled universal value function, thereby reducing variance and improving generalization; experiments on simulations and a real application show improved handling of the three identified challenges.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of ballooning Key-Value (KV) cache size and the resulting memory/time costs when LLMs process very long contexts. The key insight is that individual attention heads consistently attend to a small set of prompt positions and that this head-specific attention pattern can be predicted from a short “observation” window at the end of the prompt. SnapKV leverages this by clustering and selecting the important KV positions per head (without finetuning) and only storing those compressed KV entries during generation, yielding similar accuracy while keeping decoding latency stable and dramatically reducing memory use. Empirically, SnapKV speeds decoding ~3.6×, improves memory efficiency ~8.2× on 16K inputs, scales to ~380K tokens on a single A100 with negligible accuracy loss, and maintains baseline performance across 16 long-context datasets.

result.text: This paper addresses the problem of certifying robustness of machine learning models against data poisoning attacks that modify, delete, or insert training examples. The key insight is that bagging’s subsampling and majority-vote structure provides intrinsic, algorithm-agnostic resilience: if the number of poisoned training points is below a derived threshold, the ensemble’s majority vote cannot be flipped regardless of the base learner’s behavior. The authors prove a tight bound on that threshold (tight when no assumptions are made about the base learner), derive a certification procedure that counts how many base models’ training sets would be affected by a given tampering budget, and empirically validate the approach on MNIST and CIFAR-10—reporting, for example, 91.1% certified accuracy on MNIST against arbitrary modifications/deletions/insertions of 100 training examples.

result.text: We propose Diversity-Aware Diffusion Training (DADT), which brings formal task-diversity theory to the denoising-timestep view of diffusion models. We estimate a per-timestep diversity profile using tractable proxies (e.g., Fisher–Rao distance or relative-entropy between consecutive noising distributions and score outputs), then (i) partition timesteps into the smallest intervals whose within-cluster diversity stays below a threshold and (ii) allocate minibatch sampling probabilities proportional to each timestep’s marginal “representation gain” (diversity × gradient-variance). This yields clusters and curricula that are data-driven rather than hand-tuned and come with sample-complexity intuition: when inter-cluster diversity is high, the shared representation within each cluster is identifiable, improving convergence and reducing negative transfer. Practically, DADT plugs into existing clustered/curriculum diffusion training and routing modules and consistently speeds training and improves FID/IS without inference-time cost.

result.text: PatchComplete tackles the problem of 3D shape completion that generalizes to unseen object categories by avoiding overfitting to whole-object priors. The key insight is that local geometric substructures (multi-resolution patches) are more category-agnostic than full shapes, so learning priors over these patches captures shared parts (e.g., legs, surfaces) useful across classes. The method learns a dictionary of multi-scale patch priors from training categories, uses attention to associate and aggregate relevant priors to an input partial scan, and decodes the aggregated representation into a complete 3D shape; this patch-based design yields substantial improvements on both synthetic and real scanned data for novel-category completion.

args.text: We propose Diff-GradScribble: an active weakly supervised camouflaged object detection framework that combines diffusion-generated pseudo-mask ensembles with expected gradient-norm query selection. Starting from a scribble-supervised COD learner, we sample multiple plausible masks per image from a conditional diffusion segmenter to form a pixel-wise posterior and estimate, for each candidate pixel/short-stroke, the expected grad-norm of supervising it under this posterior; we then query the top-K locations that maximize predicted parameter change while enforcing spatial diversity. The model is retrained with the new scribbles using consistency/feature-guided losses and a diffusion-consistency regularizer that aligns discriminative predictions with the diffusion ensemble. We hypothesize this principled acquisition policy cuts scribble budgets substantially and focuses annotation on boundary-ambiguous regions, outperforming entropy/uncertainty baselines and passive scribble policies on COD10K/NC4K.

result.text: GeCoNeRF tackles the problem of training Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) from only a few input views by introducing a geometry-aware consistency regularization that supplies reliable supervisory signals at unobserved viewpoints. The key insight is to render a depth map from the current NeRF at an unobserved view, warp the sparse input images into that view using the rendered geometry, and impose feature-level (rather than pixel-level) consistency as pseudo-ground-truth so the model learns semantic and structural constraints while still permitting view-dependent radiance. Methodologically, the paper warps input-image features into novel views using NeRF-rendered depths, filters out erroneous warps with a proposed validation step, and integrates these feature-level consistency losses along with stabilization strategies during optimization to regularize few-shot NeRF training and improve reconstruction quality.

result.text: We propose a bilevel affinity-guided training scheme for diffusion models that jointly learns timestep clusters, curricula, and routing. Starting from contiguous timestep clusters initialized by SNR/affinity, we learn per-cluster curricula that prioritize harder (low-noise) steps while a lightweight routing module allocates more task-specific channels to early timesteps; within each cluster, RotoGrad-style gradient rotation and normalization reduce residual conflicts. The outer loop updates cluster memberships and curriculum weights using differentiable proxies of difficulty/relatedness (e.g., relative-entropy shifts between adjacent noising distributions), allowing clusters to merge/split as training progresses. This unifies optimization, architecture, and scheduling to mitigate negative transfer, improving convergence and sample quality without inference-time overhead.

result.text: The paper tackles the gap between practical “unlearning” procedures and true data-deletion privacy in machine learning, showing that existing unlearning guarantees are insufficient because (a) deletion requests that depend on published models induce interdependence among records so retraining alone may not protect deleted users, and (b) caching partial computations across releases can leak deleted information over time. The key insight is that protecting deleted records requires ensuring the privacy of the remaining records as well—privacy of existing data is necessary for privacy of deletions—and that sound deletion guarantees must account for adaptive deletion behavior and cumulative leakage. Building on this, the authors formalize a robust deletion notion and introduce a secure, accurate, and computationally efficient unlearning procedure based on noisy (differentially private) gradient descent that avoids reusable cached state and adds calibrated noise to gradients to prevent long-term leakage while maintaining model utility.

args.text: We propose End-to-End Timestep Credit Assignment (ETCA) for diffusion training, which estimates how errors at each denoising timestep impact downstream sampling quality and uses this to adapt optimization and capacity. Concretely, we differentiate through a lightweight surrogate of the chosen sampler and preconditioned score network to obtain per-timestep influence scores on a validation proxy, then allocate minibatch sampling, gradient modulation, and channel routing capacity in proportion to influence. The evolving influence profile induces an automatic curriculum—emphasizing globally structural low-noise steps early and fine-detail steps later—while mitigating negative transfer by restricting optimization and routing updates to high-influence, high-affinity windows. ETCA complements existing routing and curriculum techniques and improves convergence and sample quality at fixed NFEs without inference-time overhead.

result.text: The paper addresses how to provide explicit camera-motion control for pretrained video diffusion models without any task-specific finetuning or annotated datasets. Its key insight is that intermediate noisy latents of diffusion models encode a layout prior such that rearranging pixels in these latents causes corresponding spatial relocation in the decoded frames, and that camera motion can be modeled as a structured pixel rearrangement induced by perspective changes. Building on this, the authors introduce CamTrol: a two-stage, training-free pipeline that first simulates explicit image-layout rearrangement by applying camera transforms to a reconstructed 3D point cloud of an input image, then uses the sequence of rearranged images to craft corresponding noisy-latent trajectories so off-the-shelf video diffusion models generate videos exhibiting the desired camera motion; experiments show improved camera-motion alignment, generalization across base models, and capabilities for complex trajectories and unsupervised 3D video generation.

We propose CertiSelect-Unlearn: deletion-stable hyperparameter selection for machine unlearning that combines streaming IJ/approximate unlearning with bagged/hash-bagged ensembles and DP/RDP-accounted validation so that deletions up to a certified budget neither force re-tuning nor invalidate guarantees. Concretely, each base learner trains on a hash-partitioned subsample; its hyperparameters are chosen via privately noisy validation on a disjoint slice and accompanied by a stability certificate (via influence/leave-one-out style bounds) that the top choice is unchanged under removal of up to B training points; at deletion time we update only affected base learners with fixed hyperparameters and rely on counting-based ensemble certificates to preserve the majority vote. DP-based reduction from adaptive to non-adaptive deletions and honest DP tuning close the hyperparameter-selection failure mode and shrink the denial-of-service attack surface, while BILP-style collective robustness analysis yields per-input prediction and bounded-cost guarantees for the ensemble.

Ensemble disagreement also drives active scribble placement on high-uncertainty regions to minimize annotation while capturing subtle camo details. This bridges diffusion accuracy with scribble efficiency and is expected to surpass prior weakly supervised COD without full masks.

result.text: We propose Action-Conditioned Object Radiance Fields (AC-ORF) for visual RL: unsupervised object-centric 3D decomposition produces per-object radiance fields that serve as the agent’s state, and a lightweight action-conditioned dynamics head predicts how each object’s latent field transforms under executed action sequences. Compared to NeRF-supervised state learning, AC-ORF targets control-sufficient, occlusion-robust, and compositional states that support transfer from few-object tasks to many-object settings. A two-stage self-expert cloning pretrain with strong augmentations can further endow radiance latents with visual invariances before RL fine-tuning, improving zero-shot robustness to appearance shifts.

args.text: Anti-Aliased Masked Point Modeling (AA-MPM): we argue that current masked point pretraining pipelines downsample and patch irregular point clouds without anti-aliasing, causing geometric aliasing of high-frequency structures (edges, thin parts) that degrades learned representations. We insert content-adaptive graph-spectral low-pass filters on local kNN neighborhoods before each masking/downsampling stage in a pyramid encoder, aligning the passband to the target sampling lattice and modulating mask ratios by estimated local geometric bandwidth. Concretely, lightweight Chebyshev graph filters with parameters predicted from local curvature/normals or attention spectra are combined with variable-radius Poisson-disk resampling; we train with a reconstruction loss over coordinates and normals augmented by a high-frequency penalty, and optionally distill semantics from 2D/language teachers. This plug-in reduces aliasing with minimal overhead, improving robustness to density/sensor variations and boosting downstream accuracy over Point-MAE-style and locally constrained MPM baselines.

result.text: The paper addresses the high memory cost of KV caching during generative inference with large language models by proposing a plug-and-play way to compress the KV cache without retraining. The key insight is that attention heads exhibit distinct, predictable structures—some focus on local context, some on special tokens, and some attend broadly—so the cache can be adapted per-head to keep only the vectors that matter. args.text: We propose Anti-Aliased Masked Point Modeling (AA-MPM) for 3D point-cloud pretraining: before any hierarchical masking or token subsampling, we estimate each neighborhood’s spectral bandwidth (via a kNN graph Laplacian or attention-derived spectra) and apply a learned low-pass prefilter aligned to the planned sampling lattice, while selecting blue-noise–like mask patterns that satisfy a local Nyquist criterion. The encoder then operates on bandlimited, alias-minimized tokens à la Point-M2AE, and the decoder uses alias-aware synthesis filters to progressively reconstruct high-frequency details only where the estimated bandwidth supports them, reducing the need for heavy global attention as in LCM. Training adds an anti-aliasing regularizer that penalizes post-mask energy above the local Nyquist rate and a curriculum that increases mask ratios as bandwidth estimates improve, enabling higher mask rates with better transfer. This yields more stable pretraining, improved downstream accuracy, and robustness to sparsity and nonuniform sampling.

result.text: The paper addresses negative transfer in multitask learning, where disparities in task-specific gradient magnitudes and directions when updating shared parameters hurt overall performance. The key insight is that negative transfer must be treated jointly in magnitude and direction—simply rescaling gradients or greedily altering directions can fail or destabilize training—so a method should both homogenize magnitudes and rotate directions in a principled, convergent way. result.text: The paper addresses when and why representation-based transfer learning can reduce sample complexity for new tasks by learning a shared feature map from multiple related tasks. The key insight is that task diversity — a formal, general notion introduced by the authors — is the crucial property that lets a shared representation be identified from task-specific outputs, leading to a decomposition of sample complexity into representation and task-specific parts; with sufficiently diverse tasks, learning the shared representation from t tasks requires about C(H) + t C(F) samples while learning a new task using that representation requires only about C(F) samples. Methodologically, the authors formalize tasks as functions f_j ∘ h in a composite class F ∘ H, introduce a general diversity condition and prove statistical guarantees via a novel chain rule for Gaussian complexities, then instantiate the framework in several concrete models to demonstrate how the bounds apply.

result.text: The paper addresses estimation for models defined by conditional moment restrictions (e.g., nonparametric instrumental variable regression), a class of often ill-posed inverse problems where standard estimators can be unstable or rate-suboptimal. result.text: Anti-Aliased Masked Point Modeling (AA-MPM): we argue that current masked point pretraining pipelines downsample and patch irregular point clouds without anti-aliasing, causing geometric aliasing of high-frequency structures (edges, thin parts) that degrades learned representations. We insert content-adaptive graph-spectral low-pass filters on local kNN neighborhoods before each masking/downsampling stage in a pyramid encoder, aligning the passband to the target sampling lattice and modulating mask ratios by estimated local geometric bandwidth. Concretely, lightweight Chebyshev graph filters with parameters predicted from local curvature/normals or attention spectra are combined with variable-radius Poisson-disk resampling; we train with a reconstruction loss over coordinates and normals augmented by a high-frequency penalty, and optionally distill semantics from 2D/language teachers. This plug-in reduces aliasing with minimal overhead, improving robustness to density/sensor variations and boosting downstream accuracy over Point-MAE-style and locally constrained MPM baselines.

result.text: The paper addresses the fragmented landscape of graph learning by proposing a single framework that can handle node-, edge-, and graph-level tasks across generation, regression, and classification. The key insight is to recast prediction tasks as conditional generation problems, allowing diffusion models to perform deterministic predictions with theoretical guarantees and enabling a unified treatment of diverse task types. Methodologically, the authors introduce Latent Graph Diffusion (LGD), which encodes graphs into a latent space via an encoder/decoder pair, trains a diffusion model in that latent space, and supports conditioning through a cross-attention mechanism so it can jointly generate node, edge, and graph features of mixed types. Empirically, LGD achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results across many graph generation and regression benchmarks, demonstrating the practicality of treating “all tasks as generation.”

args.text: Parallax-Amodal via Training-Free Camera Diffusion Control. From a single RGB crop and its visible mask, we synthesize a short pseudo-orbit with explicit camera motion using training-free latent rearrangement in a pretrained video diffusion model, creating parallax that constrains occlusion and object extent. A slot-conditioned latent diffusion decoder completes the amodal mask by rendering depth-ordered slots across the generated views and optimizing a multi-view consensus, while retrieved shape/expansion priors steer completion from the visible region and suppress occluders. This self-supervised multi-view signal complements standard amodal supervision, improving occluder invariance and yielding calibrated uncertainty without extra annotations.

result.text: The paper tackles offline preference-based reinforcement learning, where an agent must learn from fixed trajectory data and human pairwise preferences without online interaction or explicit reward functions. Its key insight is that learning a separate scalar reward is an unnecessary information bottleneck because dynamics and task information are orthogonal, so jointly modeling trajectories and preferences can directly recover task-consistent behavior. The proposed method, Offline Preference-guided Policy Optimization (OPPO), optimizes a contextual policy via an offline hindsight information matching objective while concurrently fitting a preference model to select optimal contexts, and iteratively refines the decision policy by alternating between these two objectives. Empirically, OPPO more accurately captures preferences and outperforms baselines that rely on learned or true rewards when applied with offline RL.

result.text: Object-centric generative modeling struggles to decode slot-based representations into high-quality images and videos, producing blurry or distorted objects that limit controllable generation and editing. The key insight is to leverage the strong generative capacity of latent diffusion models (LDMs) as slot-to-image decoders, enabling more powerful, object-aware synthesis while preserving the structured slot representation. SlotDiffusion implements an object-centric LDM that conditions diffusion decoding on learned slot features (and extends to video by modeling temporal dynamics), yielding state-of-the-art unsupervised object segmentation and substantially improved image/video generation across multiple synthetic and real-world datasets. The learned slot features are also compatible with existing object-centric dynamics models, improving video prediction and temporal reasoning, and scale to complex datasets like PASCAL VOC and COCO when paired with self-supervised pre-trained encoders.

result.text: EgoDistill tackles the problem of making egocentric video understanding models feasible for resource-constrained settings by dramatically reducing their computational cost. The key insight is that rich clip-level video features produced by heavy models can be reconstructed by distilling semantics from a few sparsely sampled frames and complementary head-motion signals derived from lightweight IMU sensors, so expensive per-frame dense processing can be avoided. The method trains a student network to mimic heavy video-model features by fusing sparse visual embeddings with IMU-derived motion features, and introduces a self-supervised objective to learn robust IMU representations; at inference the student replaces the heavyweight model, yielding similar recognition accuracy with roughly 200× fewer GFLOPs.

args.text: We propose Ego-NeRF-Aug: an on-policy visual RL algorithm that learns a latent radiance-field state and regularizes the encoder by synthesizing small virtual viewpoint/light perturbations and enforcing geometry-aware, feature-level cross-view consistency at every step. Concretely, a lightweight NeRF decoder supervises the latent while GeCoNeRF-style depth-render-and-warp produces pseudo-target features at unobserved views, yielding invariances to camera and appearance shifts without extra cameras or datasets. We further perform a SECANT-like weak-to-strong self-expert cloning phase where the student is trained with strong, render-time perturbations from the latent field before on-policy fine-tuning. For compositional manipulation, we feed object-centric slots derived from the shared encoder into an entity-relational policy, enabling transfer from few-object to many-object settings under large visual OOD.

result.text: The paper addresses offline preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL), where only pairwise trajectory preferences from humans are available instead of explicit rewards, and aims to provide provable learning guarantees with general function approximation. args.text: We propose Variance-Adaptive Spectral Optimism for operator-based RL: maintain a reduced-rank RKHS approximation of the Bellman operator but construct heteroscedastic, spectrum-aware confidence sets that combine GP-style information-gain control with smoothness-proportional regularization. Concretely, we fit the operator via reduced-rank RKHS regression and track a per-eigencomponent noise recursion to form variance-scaled UCBs, then plan optimistically in the induced low-dimensional subspace while prioritizing exploration along eigencomponents by their posterior variance-to-value-influence ratio. This yields instance-dependent guarantees that scale with an operator information-gain term and effective rank (rather than ambient dimension) and, via the variance-aware analysis, can achieve logarithmic dependence on horizon. By coupling exploration to downstream value sensitivity rather than Bellman residual alone, the method targets components most impactful for control and avoids known Bellman-error pitfalls.

We propose Content-Conditioned Affinity Routing (CCAR) for diffusion training: rather than grouping denoising tasks only by timestep, we learn a small set of adapter-augmented experts and a lightweight gate g(x, t) that routes each (sample, timestep) to the expert whose content-conditioned affinity best matches its local denoising difficulty, with affinities estimated online via DADT-style diversity/gradient-variance proxies. Within each expert we mitigate residual negative transfer using RotoGrad and apply an expert-specific curriculum that emphasizes harder early timesteps for its assigned samples. An outer loop updates the gate and adaptively merges/splits experts guided by task-diversity identifiability, yielding per-sample, per-timestep routing that preserves contiguous timestep structure when appropriate but specializes for outlier content. At inference, top-1 routing adds negligible overhead and improves quality and convergence without increasing backbone size.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem that zero-shot monocular depth estimation (MDE) methods produce robust global depth layouts but lack fine detail, while diffusion-based MDE can add detail but often fails on complex real-world geometry due to limited 3D priors. The key insight is to combine strengths by using a pre-trained MDE prediction as a global depth conditioning signal and applying a conditional diffusion refiner to add high-frequency, image-consistent details without disturbing the affine-invariant global structure. The method trains a plug-and-play diffusion refiner called BetterDepth with global pre-alignment and local patch masking so the refiner learns to respect the input depth conditioning while refining detail, and it is trained efficiently on small synthetic datasets to generalize zero-shot to diverse real scenes. result.text: The paper addresses the fragmentation in computer vision where different tasks require distinct architectures and losses by asking whether diverse vision problems can be handled with a single, unified modeling interface. The key insight is that outputs of varied vision tasks (e.g., bounding boxes, masks, keypoints, captions) can all be expressed as sequences of discrete tokens, so a single pixel-to-sequence model with a shared architecture and loss can learn multiple tasks without task-specific components. Their method encodes images into a representation and uses a unified sequence decoder that, given a short prompt specifying the task, generates the appropriate token sequence for detection, segmentation, keypoint prediction, or captioning; training is performed jointly on all tasks using the same loss and tokenization scheme. result.text: Visible-slot-conditioned diffusion for amodal instance segmentation (VSDAIS). We train a latent diffusion model to complete amodal masks conditioned on the RGB crop, the detected visible mask, and an object-centric slot embedding; the slot encodes category-agnostic shape priors and is optionally augmented by retrieved expansion prototypes that steer the denoising trajectory. Synthetic occlusion layering and depth-ordered training enforce occluder invariance, while sampling multiple completions yields calibrated uncertainty and enables robust consensus masks; for videos, flow-conditioned slots impose temporal consistency. result.text: The paper addresses the approximation gap between random-feature-based attention (RFA) and exact softmax attention in efficient transformer architectures. Its key insight is that RFA can be interpreted as a sum of control-variate estimators—one per sequence element—so that softmax attention can be seen as recoverable by appropriately manipulating these control variates, enabling variance reduction. Building on this view, the authors propose a flexible, learnable control-variate form that yields a novel attention mechanism with substantially reduced approximation error while preserving RFA’s linear time and space complexity, and they validate its effectiveness across vision and language benchmarks.

args.text: We propose Deletion-Stable Recourse (DSR): counterfactual recommendations that remain valid under future unlearning of up to B training points. We train a hash-bagged ensemble and compute recourses that optimize against the worst-case label changes certified by a BILP-based collective robustness analysis, while bounding per-base-learner logit drift from deletions via influence-function/online-IJ updates and DP-noisy unlearning. A DP-based reduction converts these guarantees to the adaptive-deletion setting, and at deletion time we update only the affected base models, preserving a certified margin buffer for each issued recourse; every recourse is returned with an individualized validity budget B* and minimal-action certificate. This closes the RTBF–recourse gap by making recourses deletion-robust without retraining from scratch.

result.text: EgoTracks addresses the gap in visual object tracking benchmarks by focusing on long-term, egocentric scenarios where frequent large camera motion, hand interactions, occlusions, and rapid appearance changes make re-detection and persistent association especially challenging. We build a video latent diffusion model that decodes depth-ordered object slots into frames, where each slot carries an amodal mask and appearance; conditioning on the RGB, per-frame visible masks, and diffusion-predicted flow/depth fields enforces occlusion-aware consistency across time. result.text: The paper tackles the problem of ballooning Key-Value (KV) cache size and the resulting memory/time costs when LLMs process very long contexts. The key insight is that individual attention heads consistently attend to a small set of prompt positions and that this head-specific attention pattern can be predicted from a short “observation” window at the end of the prompt. SnapKV leverages this by clustering and selecting the important KV positions per head (without finetuning) and only storing those compressed KV entries during generation, yielding similar accuracy while keeping decoding latency stable and dramatically reducing memory use. Empirically, SnapKV speeds decoding ~3.6×, improves memory efficiency ~8.2× on 16K inputs, scales to ~380K tokens on a single A100 with negligible accuracy loss, and maintains baseline performance across 16 long-context datasets.

result.text: DeVRF addresses slow training of Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) methods for dynamic, non-rigid scenes by dramatically accelerating convergence while retaining high-fidelity novel-view synthesis. The key insight is to represent both the 3D canonical appearance and the 4D non-rigid deformation field with explicit, discrete voxel grids and to regularize the large parameter space by transferring knowledge from a separately learned multi-view static canonical volume. Methodologically, DeVRF first captures and trains a volumetric canonical radiance field from multi-view static images, then learns a voxelized 4D deformation field from few-view dynamic sequences under a static-to-dynamic learning paradigm and several implementation strategies to avoid overfitting; this yields comparable quality to prior dynamic NeRFs but trains roughly 100× faster.

result.text: The paper tackles sample-inefficient Q-function learning in continuous state-action reinforcement learning under a generative model, where classical nonparametric rates scale exponentially in the joint dimension of states and actions. The key insight is that viewing the Q-function as a kernel operator yields a Hilbert–Schmidt operator with decaying spectrum, so many practical Q-functions can be well-approximated by a low-rank operator, enabling dramatically better rates when the intrinsic rank r is small. The authors propose an iterative algorithm that alternates between low-rank matrix estimation (using a novel estimator that recovers an unknown low-rank matrix in entrywise ℓ∞ norm even with arbitrary bounded noise) and policy/value updates, and they prove this achieves sample complexity Õ(1/ε^{max(d1,d2)+2}) for γ below a threshold, an exponential improvement over classical rates; experiments on stochastic control tasks validate the approach.

result.text: We propose Diversity-Aware Diffusion Training (DADT), which brings formal task-diversity theory to the denoising-timestep view of diffusion models. We estimate a per-timestep diversity profile using tractable proxies (e.g., Fisher–Rao distance or relative-entropy between consecutive noising distributions and score outputs), then (i) partition timesteps into the smallest intervals whose within-cluster diversity stays below a threshold and (ii) allocate minibatch sampling probabilities proportional to each timestep’s marginal “representation gain” (diversity × gradient-variance). This yields clusters and curricula that are data-driven rather than hand-tuned and come with sample-complexity intuition: when inter-cluster diversity is high, the shared representation within each cluster is identifiable, improving convergence and reducing negative transfer. Practically, DADT plugs into existing clustered/curriculum diffusion training and routing modules and consistently speeds training and improves FID/IS without inference-time cost.

Building on GoalRec, we infer a trajectory-level preference model from implicit pairwise comparisons and wrap it with split-conformal quantile/CVaR uncertainty sets; planning then optimizes a risk-sensitive objective within these sets while leveraging single-policy coverage notions from offline preference RL. result.text: The paper addresses the problem of slow inference for long-context large language models, where self-attention becomes bottlenecked by loading a large key-value (KV) cache as sequence length grows. The key insight is that only a small subset of KV cache tokens are critical for a particular query and that token criticality depends on the query vector, so one can predict which cache pages matter without scanning the whole cache. They propose Quest, a query-aware KV cache page selection algorithm that maintains min/max key summaries per cache page and uses the query to estimate page criticality, loading only the top-K pages for attention; this approach yields large self-attention and end-to-end latency speedups (up to 2.23x and 7.03x respectively) with negligible accuracy loss on long-dependency tasks.

result.text: The paper tackles why masked image modeling (MIM)—a self-supervised pretraining technique that masks image regions and reconstructs them—has been effective mainly for Vision Transformers and seemingly incompatible with CNNs, limiting broad applicability. Their key insight is that MIM's benefit stems from teaching models to capture mid-level interactions among patches, which is architecture-agnostic rather than inherently transformer-specific. Experiments across standard benchmarks demonstrate that A^2MIM produces stronger, more transferable representations for diverse backbones without architecture-specific design.

The paper addresses the complexity and fragmented design choices in diffusion-based generative models that obscure which components truly drive sample quality and efficiency. Its key insight is that sampling, training, and score-network preconditioning choices can be cleanly separated into a unified design space, and that several targeted modifications across these axes—rather than wholesale architectural changes—unlock large gains in speed and fidelity. args.text: We propose World-Frame EgoDistill, which performs distillation in a stabilized 3D world coordinate system recovered from egocentric IMU and sparse keyframes. A heavy teacher runs on dense clips to produce per-frame features that are SE(3)-warped into a world grid, while a lightweight student learns to reconstruct these world-aligned features from just 1–2 keyframes plus inertial signals using a differentiable pose integrator and a 3D memory keyed by world locations. result.text: We propose CertiSelect-Unlearn: deletion-stable hyperparameter selection for machine unlearning that combines streaming IJ/approximate unlearning with bagged/hash-bagged ensembles and DP/RDP-accounted validation so that deletions up to a certified budget neither force re-tuning nor invalidate guarantees. Concretely, each base learner trains on a hash-partitioned subsample; its hyperparameters are chosen via privately noisy validation on a disjoint slice and accompanied by a stability certificate (via influence/leave-one-out style bounds) that the top choice is unchanged under removal of up to B training points; at deletion time we update only affected base learners with fixed hyperparameters and rely on counting-based ensemble certificates to preserve the majority vote. DP-based reduction from adaptive to non-adaptive deletions and honest DP tuning close the hyperparameter-selection failure mode and shrink the denial-of-service attack surface, while BILP-style collective robustness analysis yields per-input prediction and bounded-cost guarantees for the ensemble.

result.text: Visible-slot-conditioned diffusion for amodal instance segmentation (VSDAIS). We train a latent diffusion model to complete amodal masks conditioned on the RGB crop, the detected visible mask, and an object-centric slot embedding; the slot encodes category-agnostic shape priors and is optionally augmented by retrieved expansion prototypes that steer the denoising trajectory. Synthetic occlusion layering and depth-ordered training enforce occluder invariance, while sampling multiple completions yields calibrated uncertainty and enables robust consensus masks; for videos, flow-conditioned slots impose temporal consistency. This unifies visible-region-focused amodal completion, prior-guided expansion, object-centric slot modeling, and discrete diffusion-based mask generation, addressing brittleness to occluders and improving generalization.

result.text: We propose Action-Conditioned Object Radiance Fields (AC-ORF) for visual RL: unsupervised object-centric 3D decomposition produces per-object radiance fields that serve as the agent’s state, and a lightweight action-conditioned dynamics head predicts how each object’s latent field transforms under executed action sequences. Training jointly maximizes mutual information between (current object-ORF latents, action sequence) and future ORF latents via a temporal action-driven contrastive objective, while a light-field rendering head provides fast multi-view supervision and A-LIX-style encoder gradient constraints stabilize TD learning. Compared to NeRF-supervised state learning, AC-ORF targets control-sufficient, occlusion-robust, and compositional states that support transfer from few-object tasks to many-object settings. A two-stage self-expert cloning pretrain with strong augmentations can further endow radiance latents with visual invariances before RL fine-tuning, improving zero-shot robustness to appearance shifts.

result.text: The paper addresses estimation for models defined by conditional moment restrictions (e.g., nonparametric instrumental variable regression), a class of often ill-posed inverse problems where standard estimators can be unstable or rate-suboptimal. The key insight is to cast estimation as a min–max (zero-sum) game: the estimator picks a candidate from a hypothesis space while an adversary seeks moment violations over a test-function space, and regularizing the adversary by a second-moment penalty yields a principled criterion whose statistical complexity is governed by the joint “critical radius’’ of the two function classes. Methodologically, the authors analyze the resulting estimator via a novel localized Rademacher complexity for minimax objectives to derive tight estimation rates for general hypothesis and test spaces, instantiate these results for RKHS, high-dimensional sparse linear models, shape-constrained spaces, ensembles, and neural nets, and provide computationally efficient solvers (e.g., stochastic first-order methods) plus experiments demonstrating the approach.

The paper tackles the problem of reconstructing high-quality point clouds from sparse, noisy, and incomplete 3D scans by jointly addressing densification, denoising, and completion rather than treating them separately.
